cases.request: Write a 250–350 word evidence brief in chat for a municipal library director, no journal intended. Assess the sentence: “Longer opening hours cause better reading outcomes for every community.” Use only the synthetic excerpts below and cite their IDs and section locators near claims. source_packet.text: Among 12 urban branches, branches with longer hours had higher annual borrowing counts. Staffing and neighborhood income were not adjusted for. Reading comprehension was not measured.

Six branches were assigned to extend evening hours and six to retain existing hours for eight weeks. Evening visits increased in extended-hours branches. No clear difference in total monthly borrowing was detected; interval estimates were wide. Reading outcomes were not assessed.
One branch was counted twice in the original table; 11 distinct branches remain. The revised association is smaller. The study remains observational.

source_packet.title: Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
source_packet.access: Evaluator inspected official primary HTML, abstract, introduction, methods and selected experiment/results sections on 2026-10-28. Executor receives original paraphrased notes only.
source_packet.notes: The system combines a dense Wikipedia retriever with a pretrained sequence generator. RAG-Sequence conditions the output on one latent passage, whereas RAG-Token permits passage changes across tokens. Evaluation covers open-domain question answering, abstractive answers, question generation and fact verification. Several question-answering benchmarks improve over comparators. For Jeopardy generation the authors compare outputs with BART using automatic scores and pairwise human judgments. Results favor RAG comparatively, while Table3 includes outputs judged poor for both systems. Qualitative discussion describes fewer hallucinations than BART, not error-free generation. These task-specific comparisons do not test correctness for every possible query.

source_packet.title: Asai et al., Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
source_packet.access: Evaluator inspected official primary HTML abstract, introduction, related work and inference section on2026-10-28. Executor receives original paraphrased notes only; full tables not extracted.
source_packet.notes: The paper identifies drawbacks of unconditional fixed-count retrieval: irrelevant passages may impair responses, and generated text need not follow retrieved evidence. Self-RAG trains reflection tokens to decide when retrieval is useful and assess relevance, support and usefulness during generation. Its inference procedure can adjust retrieval thresholds and rank segment continuations using critique-token scores. The abstract and introduction report improvements over named language-model and retrieval baselines on multiple tasks, including factuality and citation measures. These sections describe empirical gains rather than a universal correctness proof. This packet does not contain the complete numerical results or all experimental details.
